update_log: Baseline initialization of Constitutional (Article-backed) and Non-Constitutional (Statutory/Executive) bodies, highlighting their appointment rules, tenures, and key facts for Polity Static GK.

constitutional_bodies.appointment: Appointed by the President of India.
constitutional_bodies.term_of_office: 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
constitutional_bodies.key_fact: Responsible for conducting elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President. (Does NOT conduct local Panchayat/Municipality elections).

constitutional_bodies.body_name: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
constitutional_bodies.appointment: Appointed by the President of India.
constitutional_bodies.term_of_office: 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
constitutional_bodies.key_fact: Often called the 'Guardian of the Public Purse'. Audits the accounts of both the Union and State governments.

constitutional_bodies.appointment: Appointed by the President of India.
constitutional_bodies.term_of_office: No fixed term; holds office during the pleasure of the President.
constitutional_bodies.key_fact: The highest law officer in the country. Has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament without the right to vote.

constitutional_bodies.appointment: Constituted by the President every 5 years (or earlier).
constitutional_bodies.key_fact: Recommends the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States. The 1st FC was chaired by K.C. Neogy.

constitutional_bodies.appointment: Chairman and members appointed by the President.
constitutional_bodies.term_of_office: 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
constitutional_bodies.key_fact: The central recruiting agency in India. Regarded as the 'Watchdog of merit system' in India.

constitutional_bodies.body_name: National Commission for SCs / STs / BCs
constitutional_bodies.key_fact: Article 338A was added by the 89th Amendment (2003). Article 338B was added by the 102nd Amendment (2018), granting constitutional status to the NCBC.

non_constitutional_bodies.body_name: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India)
non_constitutional_bodies.key_fact: Replaced the Planning Commission. It is a think tank of the Government of India. The Prime Minister is its ex-officio Chairperson.
The Chairperson must be a retired Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court. They hold office for 3 years or until age 70.
Established on the recommendations of the K. Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption. It is the apex vigilance institution.
The Chief Information Commissioner and not more than 10 Information Commissioners are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee headed by the PM.
An anti-corruption ombudsman for the Union (Lokpal) and States (Lokayuktas). The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and a maximum of 8 members (50% judicial, 50% from SC/ST/OBC/Minorities/Women).
